title: Applied ML Evals: Integration and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Asha Verma
content:
Purpose
This playbook documents the integrated process we use to onboard models into production, validate prompt sets and benchmarks, apply quantization profiles, and triage regressions using the eval harness. It is intended for ML engineers, applied researchers, and platform owners responsible for model serving quality at Redwood Inference.

Scope
- Applies to: all models served via Redwood hosted and dedicated runtimes.
- Includes: eval harness configuration, prompt-set design, benchmark definition, quantization validation, and regression triage flow.
- Excludes: model training workflows and external third-party model providers (unless explicitly onboarded via the model-onboarding checklist).

Key objectives
- Ensure consistent, repeatable onboarding that prevents quality regressions.
- Provide clear thresholds and guardrails for automated and manual rollouts.
- Minimize false positives/negatives in regression detection by combining statistical and example-based checks.

Owner & responsibilities
- Playbook owner: Applied ML Platform (applied-ml subteam).
- Point-of-contact: Asha Verma (applied-ml-platform).
- Review cadence: Quarterly or when a major change to the eval harness, quantization library, or runtime occurs.

Roles
1. Model Owner (ML engineer): prepare model artifacts, provide expected behavior doc, and run initial evals.
2. Eval Engineer (Applied ML): author eval harness config, create prompt sets, and implement thresholds.
3. Platform Owner (Infra/Runtime): ensure quantization and runtime compatibility, manage canary capacity.
4. Incident Owner (SRE/Product): lead triage and coordinate rollback/fix.

Onboarding checklist (high-level)
1. Readiness review
   - Confirm model license and security classification.
   - Verify model format (ONNX/FP16/quantized artifact) and required runtimes.
   - Confirm expected sequence length and KV cache behavior.
2. Eval harness integration
   - Create eval config in eval-harness repo: name, model_id, task tags, dataset references.
   - Define metric suite: accuracy/EM, BLEU, ROUGE, F1, perplexity, hallucination rate, toxicity scores, latency P50/P95.
3. Prompt sets & benchmarks
   - Curate core prompt-set: 200–2000 representative prompts across high-priority use-cases.
   - Create gold labels/expected outputs where applicable.
   - Define benchmark baseline using the current production model.
4. Quantization plan
   - Identify candidate quant profiles (8-bit, mixed-precision).
   - Run quantization validation benchmark: functional tests and distributional shift checks.
5. Canary rollout & monitoring
   - Canary on 1–5% traffic for 24–72 hours with strict monitoring (see Monitoring section).
   - Use automated rollback criteria (regression > threshold) and manual gate for low-frequency but high-impact failures.

Eval harness configuration (examples)
- Standard eval config fields (as YAML in repo):

  name: "sales-assistant-v1-onboarding"
  model_id: "redwood/open-model-x-quant-8bit"
  tasks: ["qa", "summarization", "classification"]
  prompt_set: "sales-assistant-core-2026-11"
  metrics: ["exact_match", "f1", "rouge_l", "toxicity_score"]
  variants:
    - name: "baseline"
      model_ref: "prod:open-model-x:2026-10-01"
    - name: "candidate"
      model_ref: "candidate:open-model-x-quant-8bit:2026-11-30"

- Recommended runtime knobs in eval harness run: batch_size=1–8, sequence_truncation=2048, seed=42.

Prompt sets & benchmark guidelines
- Prompt taxonomy: map prompts to intent buckets (e.g., factual-recall, instruction-following, multi-step reasoning, system-instructions).
- Minimum prompt coverage: ensure at least 10 prompts per bucket and cover tail cases.
- Label quality: each gold label should have an owner and an annotation timestamp. Use pairwise annotation for ambiguous prompts.
- Benchmark baseline: always run candidate vs production A/B; capture both automated metrics and per-example diffs for manual review.

Quality guardrails and thresholds
- Primary thresholds (default):
  - Overall automated regression flag if any of: F1 drop >= 3.0 points absolute AND p-value < 0.05, or increase in hallucination rate >= 2.5%.
  - Latency SLO: P95 generation latency <= 350 ms for <1k tokens workloads; alert if P95 > 450 ms.
  - Token cost delta: candidate > baseline by 15% => require business approval.
  - Safety: any increase in toxicity_score > 1.0 point or new category of policy violation => block rollout.
- Tiered severity: critical (safety/integrity), high (significant metric regression), medium (performance/cost), low (cosmetic or small diff).

Quantization profiles & validation steps
1. Profile selection
   - Maintain a catalog of quant profiles: e.g., q8_int8_per_channel, q4_mixed_float16, q5_dynamic.
   - Document supported layers and known exceptions per architecture.
2. Validation battery
   - Functional evals: run prompt-set benchmarks and ensure functional metric delta within thresholds.
   - Distributional checks: compare token distribution and logit-range histograms between baseline and candidate.
   - Determinism tests: run 50 repeated inferences with fixed seed and compare top-3 probabilities distribution.
3. Performance validation
   - Measure latency (P50/P95), GPU utilization, and memory footprint.
   - Verify KV cache correctness for long-history scenarios.
4. Release criteria
   - Quant candidate passes functional and safety checks, and cost/latency benefits meet expectations.

Regression triage workflow
1. Detection
   - Automated monitors (eval harness scheduled jobs and production sampling) produce regression alerts.
   - Alerts include: metric diffs, per-example failing prompts, and diff visualization.
2. Initial triage (SLAs)
   - Triage within 2 business hours for high/critical alerts.
   - Gather artifacts: eval config, raw model outputs, baseline outputs, environment snapshot (runtime version, quant profile, hardware).
3. Reproduce and scope
   - Re-run failing prompts locally with both baseline and candidate under identical runtime configs.
   - If non-deterministic or flaky, increase sample size and add randomized seeds.
4. Classification
   - Root cause categories: model-quality (training/coverage), quantization-induced, runtime bug, prompt-engineering/regression in prompts, dataset drift, infra/failure.
5. Remediation & prioritization
   - Safety/critical: immediate rollback to last good model; open high-priority bug with SRE and applied-ml.
   - High: issue to model owner for fix/rollback; consider patch release and narrow canary.
   - Medium/Low: schedule fix in next sprint; monitor for impact.
6. Postmortem
   - For critical/high: produce a postmortem with timeline, impact, RCA, action items, and owners within 3 business days.

Automated rollback criteria (examples)
- Trigger automatic rollback if any of the following are true during canary:
  - Safety violation detected by the safety classifier (new policy category) in >0.1% of sampled requests.
  - Functional regression: F1 drop >= 5 points and supported by at least 200 prompt examples.
  - Latency: P95 > 2x baseline for production traffic segment.

Monitoring & dashboards (what to surface)
- Eval harness dashboard: per-task metrics, per-prompt diffs, statistical significance, and per-variant comparison.
- Production sampling: percent of sampled requests, top failing prompts, safety classifier signals, hallucination heuristic counts.
- Infra metrics: GPU utilization, memory OOMs, runtime errors, queue latency.
- Cost metrics: tokens per request, cost per 1k tokens, and unit economics delta vs baseline.

Runbook: Canary → Promote → Rollback (step-by-step)
1. Canary start
   - Deploy candidate to canary pool (1–5%). Configure tagging: canary=true.
   - Start hourly eval-harness job against canary pool for first 24 hours.
2. Observe
   - Monitor safety, functional, latency, and cost for threshold breaches.
   - Collect manual spot-checks of per-example diffs every 6 hours.
3. Decision gates (after 24–72h)
   - Promote if no guardrail breaches and business KPIs are satisfied.
   - Extend canary if marginal regressions present but fix is likely in-flight.
   - Rollback immediately if critical guardrails breached.
4. Promotion
   - Incrementally increase traffic allocation (5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) with 24h observation windows between steps.

Examples: CLI snippets and SQL queries
- Run eval harness locally:
  $ eval-harness run --config configs/sales-assistant-v1.yaml --variant candidate --output results/candidate-vs-baseline --seed 42

- Query failing prompts from results table (example):
  SELECT prompt_id, metric_name, baseline_value, candidate_value, delta
  FROM eval_results
  WHERE delta < -0.03
  ORDER BY delta ASC
  LIMIT 200;

Best practices & tips
- Start with small, high-quality prompt-sets that reflect core user intents before expanding to long-tail cases.
- Use per-example diffs for debugging; aggregate metrics can hide systematic failures.
- Prefer conservative quant profiles early in onboarding (e.g., per-channel 8-bit) and iterate toward aggressivecompression.
- Keep safety classifiers and hallucination heuristics up-to-date with monthly retraining or rule updates.

- Prompt set guidelines: /applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks-guidelines-2026
- Quantization profiles catalog: /applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026
